evidence.quote: let ensureNotBlocked activity memberId (library: Library) : Result<unit, LendingError> =

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The block rule for borrowing, holds and renewals is decided in Tier 2 (Accounts.ensureNotBlocked, called from Loans.borrow, Holds.place and Loans.renew). Tier 3 views ask Accounts.isBlocked and do not re-derive the rule. The CLI only branches on the Blocked flag it gets from the view. The change also deletes the CLI's own owed>=5.00 check, so Tier 4 no longer decides the borrow block.

evidence.quote: | Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is added below Tier 4. Renew and standing go through the existing commit/query helpers, which use the Store and Clock ports. The change removes CLI code that loaded and saved the store directly and called Tier 2 Loans.renew, so decisions are now pure and the effects go through the edge's ports.

evidence.quote: let isBlocked memberId (library: Library) = owed memberId library >= Policy.blockingBalance
blocked until it is below {money Policy.blockingBalance}

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The blocking amount has one definition (Policy.blockingBalance), and every use, including the Tier 3 refusal text, points to it. But the new ensureNotBlocked writes the block condition again as 'owes < Policy.blockingBalance' instead of calling the existing isBlocked ('>= Policy.blockingBalance'). The two copies agree today but are separate predicates.

evidence.quote: blocked until it is below {money balance}

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The per-type blocking balance is defined in Tier 2 Policy and applied in Tier 2 Accounts. Tier 3 only shows the balance carried in the MemberBlocked error and asks isBlocked for members and standing. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code re-decides it.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change is purely about domain values and adds no new effect anywhere. The Tier 2 lookup it adds is a pure read of the Library value. Effects still go through the existing ports.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The per-type amounts have one definition (Policy.blockingBalance memberType), and the refusal text uses the value carried in the error rather than restating it. But the block condition is still in two places, isBlocked (>=) and ensureNotBlocked (<), and both had to be edited for this change. They agree, but they are copies that can drift.
